samples.summary: The five new `NoteEditorAPI` list-mutation methods dispatch document changes with no read-only/editable check, unlike the other guarded write path in the same file
samples.evidence: `initialize()` protects writes two ways: `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:413) — which only blocks *user* input, not programmatic `view.dispatch` — and an explicit mount-time opt-out for the other API-level write path, `const uploadImage = readOnly ? undefined : options.uploadImage` + `insertImageFiles: (files) => { if (!uploadImage) return; ... }` (editor.ts:240, 587). The new `toggleBulletList/toggleOrderedList/toggleTaskList/indentList/outdentList` entries (editor.ts:582-586) get neither: they call into `list-commands.ts`, which dispatches unconditionally (`replacePrefixes` → `view.dispatch`, list-commands.ts ~line 236). The preview toggle path *was* guarded (`onToggleTask: readOnly ? undefined : ...`, editor.ts:258) and the new input handler checks both `view.state.readOnly` and the `editable` facet (checkbox-input.ts:24-30), so the toolbar commands are the odd ones out. Today the only caller gates itself (`canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"`, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:252), so the bypass needs a second caller (or a future read-only-aware surface) to be reachable; note also that the owner route never passes `readOnly` at all (notes-detail.tsx:207-213). Same shape as the pre-existing `toggleBold`/`insertTable` entries, so a reviewer may consider it pre-existing — but the diff adds five more of them.

samples.summary: `computeActiveFormats` is now O(selected lines + upward scan) and it runs on every keystroke and every selection change
samples.evidence: `computeActiveFormats` gained `computeListState(state)` (commands.ts:64), which calls `selectedLines()` — parsing **every line the selection covers** — and `itemAbove`/`parentOf`, which walk backwards line by line (list-commands.ts). Its callers are hot paths that the diff does not touch: `EditorView.updateListener` fires it on every `docChanged || selectionSet` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:423), the undo/redo path calls it (editor.ts:328), and the toolbar re-derives state from it on each callback (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:243-248). With a select-all (or any large multi-line selection) on a big note, every keystroke now parses the whole selected region with a regex per line, where before the work was O(1) around the cursor.

samples.summary: `cursor: pointer` on `li.task-list-item` inherits into regions the click handler deliberately refuses to toggle
samples.evidence: `cursor` is an inherited property, so the new rule `.note-preview.note-tasks-interactive li.task-list-item { cursor: pointer }` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-preview.css:344) also paints a pointer over descendants of a task item that `onTaskClick` explicitly bails on: a nested plain `<li>` under a task (`if (clickedItem && clickedItem !== item) return;`, packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:300) and the body of a `<details>` foldout nested in a task item (`if (target.closest('a, button, details')) return;`, preview.ts:289 — a case the diff's own test at preview.test.ts covers as *not* toggling). The CSS advertises clickability the handler does not provide; the selector needs narrowing (or the handler widening).

samples.summary: Dropping `label: true` changes the rendered DOM for read-only previews too, where nothing replaces the label
samples.evidence: `md` is a module-level singleton shared by every `NotePreview` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:26), so `md.use(taskLists, { enabled: true })` (preview.ts:53, previously `{ label: true, enabled: false }`) removes the `<label>`/`for=` association from *all* previews — including the share-link read-only mount, which re-disables the boxes and attaches no click handler at all (`<NotesView readOnly={readOnly} viewMode={readOnly ? "view" : "both"} />`, packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:352; `onToggleTask` omitted at editor.ts:258). The stated justification for removing the label — "the whole item is already a click target" — only holds on interactive mounts, so read-only viewers lose the labelled checkbox without gaining the item-wide target.

samples.summary: `NoteListKind` is re-exported from the package barrel but no consumer imports it
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/index.ts:27 adds `export type { NoteListKind } from './view/list-commands.js';`, but the only consumer of the new state compares raw string literals instead (`formats.list === "bullet" | "ordered" | "task"`, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:302-316) and no file outside `list-commands.ts`/`index.ts` references the name. Either import it at the consumer or drop the barrel export.
searchedFor: knip.json workspace config (packages/notes not listed; default entry src/index.ts)

finding.summary: The five new `NoteEditorAPI` list-mutation methods dispatch document changes with no read-only/editable check, unlike the other guarded write path in the same file
finding.evidence: `initialize()` protects writes two ways: `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:413) — which only blocks *user* input, not programmatic `view.dispatch` — and an explicit mount-time opt-out for the other API-level write path, `const uploadImage = readOnly ? undefined : options.uploadImage` + `insertImageFiles: (files) => { if (!uploadImage) return; ... }` (editor.ts:240, 587). The new `toggleBulletList/toggleOrderedList/toggleTaskList/indentList/outdentList` entries (editor.ts:582-586) get neither: they call into `list-commands.ts`, which dispatches unconditionally (`replacePrefixes` → `view.dispatch`, list-commands.ts ~line 236). The preview toggle path *was* guarded (`onToggleTask: readOnly ? undefined : ...`, editor.ts:258) and the new input handler checks both `view.state.readOnly` and the `editable` facet (checkbox-input.ts:24-30), so the toolbar commands are the odd ones out. Today the only caller gates itself (`canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"`, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:252), so the bypass needs a second caller (or a future read-only-aware surface) to be reachable; note also that the owner route never passes `readOnly` at all (notes-detail.tsx:207-213). Same shape as the pre-existing `toggleBold`/`insertTable` entries, so a reviewer may consider it pre-existing — but the diff adds five more of them.

verdict.reason: The code shape is as described (editor.ts:581-585 wire the five list commands with no read-only check, and list-commands.ts:212-219 dispatches unconditionally), but the lens requires a reachable entry point that bypasses the read-only guard, and no such site exists. Repo-wide grep for the five method names returns only their definitions (list-commands.ts:255-286), the API wiring (editor.ts:581-585), unit tests, and exactly one production consumer: notes-toolbar.tsx:303,310,317,324,331 — all inside the `{canFormat && editor && ...}` block where `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"` (notes-toolbar.tsx:252,257). Of the two notes mounts, notes-detail.tsx:198-213 passes no `readOnly` to either NotesView or NotesToolbar (writable editor, gate consistent), and the only `readOnly={true}` mount, shared-document.tsx:352 (`readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, line 323), renders no toolbar and no `onEditorReady`, so no caller in that surface ever holds a NoteEditorAPI. No other package consumes @wafflebase/notes (frontend-only alias, vite.config.ts:229). The finding itself concedes the bypass "needs a second caller (or a future read-only-aware surface) to be reachable"; every existing entry point passes through the caller-side guard, so this is already-guarded, and the residual API-consistency point with insertImageFiles/onToggleTask is design-fit, not a reachable guard bypass.

finding.summary: Foldout-in-task exemption only covers <summary>; a click in the <details> BODY still ticks the task line
finding.evidence: The delta adds `summary` to the owned-control allowlist (preview.ts:276) precisely because a `<details>` block can nest inside a task `<li>` — the new test at packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:196 asserts `summary.closest('li.task-list-item')` is non-null for `- [ ] todo\n\n  <details>…`. But the only structural guard after it is `const clickedItem = target.closest('li'); if (clickedItem && clickedItem !== item) return;` (preview.ts:297-298), which exempts nested list items only. The paragraph text inside the foldout body ("body" in that same fixture) is not an `li`, not an `a/button/summary`, and not a checkbox, so `target.closest('.task-list-item')` resolves it to the enclosing task item and the handler falls through to `this.onToggleTask?.(line, checked)` (preview.ts:317) → `setTaskChecked` (editor.ts:260), silently rewriting and syncing a task line the user never pointed at. The reasoning the diff gives for the summary exemption ("toggling would edit a line nobody pointed at") applies unchanged to the folded body, and the details plugin registers its rule with `alt: [… 'list']` (details-plugin.ts:105), so this nesting is a supported source shape. Same class of bypass for any non-`li` block nested in a task item (blockquote, table cell text).

verdict.reason:
The finding claims the owned-control allowlist exempts only `summary`, leaving a click in the
body to fall through to onToggleTask. The repository code does not match: preview.ts:278 is `if (target.closest('a, button, details')) return;` — the whole `
` element is exempt, so any descendant click (including the body paragraph) returns before reaching `this.onToggleTask?.(line, checked)` at preview.ts:319. The comment at preview.ts:272-277 states the whole disclosure is exempt "not just its `summary`". The cited test also already covers the body case: preview.test.ts:213-222 clicks the `

` containing "body" inside `details.note-details` and asserts `defaultPrevented === false` and no toggles. details-plugin.ts:59/110 confirms a real `

` tag is emitted, so `closest('details')` resolves for the nested-in-list shape. The trailing generalisation about blockquote/table-cell text is the deliberate whole-item click target documented at preview.ts:252-254, not the cited evidence and not a bypass of a new guard.

finding.summary: New mutating API methods (list toggles, indent/outdent) and `setTaskChecked` dispatch without the read-only guard the sibling new code applies, and the notes editor never sets `EditorState.readOnly`
finding.evidence: `noteCheckboxInput` explicitly refuses to write when the doc is read-only or the view is non-editable (packages/notes/src/view/checkbox-input.ts:25-30), but the five new `NoteEditorAPI` methods wired at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:581-585 call `toggleBulletList`/`indentList`/… which dispatch unconditionally (packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:228-231, 289-299), as does `setTaskChecked` (list-commands.ts:290+). A grep for `EditorState.readOnly` across packages shows the editor only ever sets `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (editor.ts:413) — never the read-only facet — so `view.dispatch` from these commands mutates and syncs a read-only note. Today the only host that mounts read-only (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:352) renders no notes toolbar and never takes the API via `onEditorReady`, so I could not confirm a live caller; the exposure is that the API surface, which is public from `@wafflebase/notes`, now has more unguarded mutation entry points than before. Fix belongs on the new commands (or by adding `EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)` in editor.ts).

verdict.reason: The mechanical absence is real (list-commands.ts dispatches with no read-only check; editor.ts sets only EditorView.editable, never EditorState.readOnly), but there is no reachable bypass, which is what this lens requires. A repo-wide grep for the five new symbols yields exactly one production caller: notes-toolbar.tsx:300-334, where all five buttons sit inside `{canFormat && editor && ...}` with `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"` (notes-toolbar.tsx:252) — in read-only mode they are not rendered. The only read-only mount, shared-document.tsx:352, passes no `onEditorReady`, so notes-view.tsx:134 hands the NoteEditorAPI to nobody and renders no toolbar; the sole NotesToolbar mount (notes-detail.tsx:198-206) is the writable route and passes no readOnly. `setTaskChecked` is not on NoteEditorAPI at all (interface at editor.ts:120-206) and its only call site is explicitly readOnly-guarded at editor.ts:258-260, so that part of the evidence is factually wrong. No keymap reaches these commands (editor.ts:361-390 binds only indentWithTab/Escape; historyKeymap is [] when readOnly). Finally, no contract changed for existing consumers: the eight pre-existing toolbar commands in commands.ts also contain no readOnly check, so read-only enforcement in this package has always lived at the host boundary. Hardening the commands for a hypothetical future embedder of @wafflebase/notes is defensive design, not a broken or bypassing call site.
